title: Application prefetch files
whyItMatters: Prefetch files record which executables ran and when. They give a timeline of application use even after the programs are removed.
source: SANS Windows forensic poster: %SystemDrive%/Windows/Prefetch (*.pf execution files)
notes: Machine-wide folder, so elevation is required. Only .pf files are counted; their embedded path and run-count data is never parsed.

cleanup.risk: Prefetch is a cache Windows writes and manages itself, so it holds no documents to remove. Deleting the files by hand only slows the next program starts and Windows writes them again.
cleanup.reason: Windows creates and rebuilds these files itself to speed up program starts. There is no supported setting to clear them, and a reset of this PC is what removes them.
cleanup.source: Microsoft Learn, What is Application Launch Prefetching?: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/archive/blogs/chadduffey/what-is-application-launch-prefetching
